transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-08-26, Start: 11:00 AM ET, Duration: 55m. Attendees: Liam Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Ellen Torres (Redwood CSM); Derek Huang, Sofia Reyes, Tom Patel, Jenna Morris (Mariner Labs).

Summary: Quick console walkthrough focused on per-route usage telemetry, cost attribution and playbook suggestions. Customer wants to understand how to split traffic, what routes cost, and confirmation about VPC/private deployment constraints and data retention.

Topics: console navigation; per-route dashboards; route tagging and mapping to product teams; prefix / KV cache explanation (spoken as K V cache); batching & latency tradeoffs; private deployment and KMS; pilot plan and next steps.

00:00 Liam Carter: Alright everyone thanks for joining, I'm Liam from Redwood, I'll run the console demo with Priya and then we'll jump into specifics about cost mapping for Mariner Labs
00:18 Derek Huang: hey thanks, excited to see how this maps to our different product routes — we have 8 routes in prod, two big ones for chat and a bunch of small classification endpoints
00:32 Priya Shah: cool, super. quick qual — what are your current qps and p95 latencies? and are you running on GCP or AWS?
00:42 Sofia Reyes: we're on AWS, mostly in us-east-1, baseline qps around 60 sustained and spikes to 300 during batch runs; p95 is around 450 ms for the chat route now
00:55 Priya Shah: great, that's helpful. also curious about retention — do you need message history kept on Redwood side?
01:05 Tom Patel: we can't retain PII, so we want no retention by default and then the option to store de-identified logs for debug for 30 days, security will gate that
01:20 Jenna Morris: yes, SOC two compliance is required, we also want to understand K M S integration for key management and whether logs go to our SIEM
01:32 Liam Carter: totally reasonable. we have a SOC 2 report excerpt we'll send, and Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS for encrypting model contexts and audit logs can stream to your SIEM — we'll include integration notes.

05:10 Priya Shah: ok jumping into console — this is the main Usage Overview, shows token volume, request counts, and a heatmap by region. you'll see we group by route name, model variant, and deployment type (hosted/dedicated/private). note: some labels in the demo are synthetic.
05:34 Priya Shah: here on the left is the routes list — you can tag routes by product team, by environment, or by billing owner. Mariner could tag chat-prod, classify-prod, enrichment-worker etc. tagging maps into the cost breakdown.
06:02 Derek Huang: can we import existing route names from our gateway? we have an API gateway with internal route ids
06:10 Priya Shah: yes, we support automatic route discovery via the agent or a short mapping csv, and there's a webhook-based sync if you want continuous mapping. we'll help with the mapping during the pilot.

08:00 Priya Shah: now per-route dashboard — each route shows token breakdown, average tokens per request, median latency, cold vs warm KV cache hits (we sometimes show this as KV hit ratio), and effective cost per 1k tokens. the cost model here includes infra (GPU secs) + model multipliers + quantum of batching.
08:28 Tom Patel: that 'effective cost per 1k tokens' — can you break how you compute infra vs model costs? our FinOps wants line items
08:36 Priya Shah: absolutely — infra is derived from GPU-slices consumed (we convert to $/GPU-sec), plus model cost is a model multiplier. there's an export to csv that shows the decomposition per time window.

10:05 Priya Shah: demoing the routing policy page — you can set fallbacks, prioritize by latency or cost, region failover, and a route-level canary. for example you can route low-latency traffic to a dedicated pool and low-cost traffic to hosted.
10:28 Derek Huang: curious about fallback — if the dedicated pool is saturated, does Redwood auto-fallback to hosted, and does that preserve K V cache?
10:40 Priya Shah: good question. fallback can be configured to a compatible model variant; KV cache isn't shared across variants or pools, so warm cache benefits are best within the same pool. we'll show quantized model variants as the fallback, so latency will increase slightly but cost drops.

13:12 Priya Shah: here's the batching suggestion engine — based on your latency SLO and request size distribution we recommend batch sizes and max_latency ms. it simulates estimated cost savings and expected p95 impact. note: simulation uses historical traffic shape you upload.
13:45 Tom Patel: is batching safe for chat? we have streaming responses and some routes need sub-200 ms p95, batching sounds like it could add latency
13:55 Priya Shah: yes for streaming chat we tend to keep batches small or use continuous batching modes; for non-streaming classification it's usually a big win. we'll configure per-route policies.

16:30 Priya Shah: switching to the Cost Attribution view — you can create allocation rules: tag-based allocation (by product tag), volume-proportional, or custom split tables. you can also set manual chargebacks by percentage for shared models.
16:58 Tom Patel: for shared models across teams can we do a weighted split based on token type? e.g., system vs user tokens — our internal billing wants user token only
17:10 Priya Shah: yep you can split by token-type if your proxy marks tokens in metadata; we parse metadata and apply rules. otherwise we can run a mapping job during pilot.

19:00 Priya Shah: pulling up Live Playbook — a recipe for when a route's cost-per-1k rises above threshold. it triggers suggestions like enable prefix caching, lower beam size, swap to quantized variant, or set temporary rate limit. it's not automatic unless you enable auto-remediation.
19:28 Derek Huang: auto-remediation — do you have guardrails? we don't want degraded model quality in production
19:37 Priya Shah: yes there's an approval flow and you can run the action in dry-run mode first. plus there are quality monitors tied to eval prompt sets; if quality drops beyond a set delta, the system rolls back.

22:10 Priya Shah: now private deployment notes — for V P C/private we run a customer control plane that talks over a secure tunnel, and you can run inference nodes on-prem or in your VPC. K M S integration supports your HSM or cloud KMS. small caveat: some kernel optimizations are hardware-specific so latency profiles vary by host.
22:40 Jenna Morris: on that, does private mean we control the logs? we require audit logs to be stored for 12 months in our S3 under our account
22:52 Liam Carter: yes, for Private you manage the logging destination. we'll forward a sample log schema and retention config.

25:05 Priya Shah: back to console — here's the anomalies tab — it surfaces sudden jumps in token rate or effective cost per route; it tries to classify root cause (traffic spike vs model degradation vs batching change). it's heuristic and sometimes noisy.
25:38 Derek Huang: can we plug in our own anomaly detector? we have a Prometheus + Grafana stack for infra alerts
25:45 Priya Shah: you can export telemetry to your monitoring endpoints via webhook, or push to S3 and run your tooling. we also have a metrics exporter for Datadog/Prometheus.

28:10 Priya Shah: sharing the Benchmarks link in the chat — (link: https://s.redwood.ai/benchmarks-mariner-sample) — this spreadsheet contains token/latency TCO sims and sample batch configs.
28:28 Tom Patel: thanks, we'll look. can Redwood run a short benchmark with our sample payloads to provide apples-to-apples numbers?
28:40 Priya Shah: yes, Priya will run a 1-hour benchmark against hosted and a sample dedicated profile, using your payloads. we'll share results and a recommended config.

31:00 Priya Shah: quick note about transcription reliability — sometimes the console shows KV cache hits as K V hits and our auto-transcription writes it oddly in the logs — ignore that in the UI.
31:22 Derek Huang: ha, noted. a weird question — does Redwood charge for cache warmups or only for token generation?
31:32 Priya Shah: costs are token+infra based. cache warmups incur infra time (GPU sec) if we warm a model, so it's reflected in infra line item. prefix caching that avoids generation reduces token cost.

34:05 Priya Shah: demoing route-level drilldown — here you can replay traffic using anonymized payloads and see expected cost delta if you toggled batching, model variant, or enable prefix caching. it's useful to preview impact before changing production.
34:30 Sofia Reyes: how accurate are those previews? we need +/- 10% for planning
34:38 Priya Shah: typically within 10-15% depending on traffic variance and cold-start incidence. we'll run real benchmarks to refine those numbers during pilot.

37:00 Liam Carter: circling back — Mariner had the constraint that security needs on-prem logging and SAML SSO integration, right?
37:12 Jenna Morris: yes SAML, and SCIM for provisioning, and also role-based access control — we want fine-grained RBAC by team
37:22 Ellen Torres: we support SAML SSO and SCIM, and RBAC can be customized per team and route. I'll share our SAML metadata example.

40:00 Priya Shah: here's the Audit Log sample — shows who did what (route edits, routing policy changes). we can push these logs to your S3 or to an event streaming endpoint.
40:20 Jenna Morris: are logs tamper-evident? we need chain-of-custody for some audits
40:28 Liam Carter: we can provide signed log bundles and timestamping integrations — we'll include the details in the security pack.

43:00 Priya Shah: showing the Optimize tab — model/quantization suggestions based on historical accuracy and latency. it suggests a quantized int8 variant for some of your non-chat routes and flags potential quality regressions for manual review.
43:25 Derek Huang: curious about quality monitoring — how is regression detection done?
43:32 Priya Shah: we tie eval prompt sets to routes, collect a small sample of responses, compute functional metrics (F1/EM or domain-specific scoring), and raise a regression alert when delta exceeds your threshold. you can mark prompts as critical vs non-critical.

46:00 Priya Shah: demo wrap-up — pilot options: Hosted trial (fastest), Dedicated reserved pool 2 GPU nodes for predictable latency, or Private for on-prem. Given your security posture, many companies start with Hosted pilot + security review and then transition to Dedicated or Private.
46:25 Tom Patel: pricing — rough monthly for dedicated 2-node pool vs hosted pay-as-you-go?
46:33 Liam Carter: we'll send a tailored pricing sheet but rough math: dedicated has a fixed monthly for reserved capacity which lowers $/token for high volume; hosted is variable and fine for pilots. we'll show sample TCO in the spreadsheet.

49:10 Derek Huang: last question: how do we instrument route-level sampling so that we can later chargeback to product teams? is that just tags?
49:22 Priya Shah: tags plus sampling rules — you can sample a percentage of requests and include product metadata; console then attributes costs based on sample expansion or full traffic if metadata is present.

52:00 Liam Carter: ok let's recap next steps — we'll provision a trial key and a sandbox routes mapping file, Priya will run a benchmark with your sample payloads, Ellen will send SOC2 excerpt and SAML config, and I'll put together the pricing/TCO.
52:28 Derek Huang: perfect, appreciate the specificity. can we get a calendar invite for the security deep-dive?
52:36 Ellen Torres: yes I'll send a calendar invite for 2026-09-03 10am ET and include our security lead.

54:10 Jenna Morris: thanks everyone, that was helpful. looking forward to the security doc and the benchmark.
54:22 Liam Carter: thanks Mariner team, we'll follow up with the artifacts and action items. talk soon.

End of transcript.

Referenced artifacts in chat: https://s.redwood.ai/benchmarks-mariner-sample (benchmarks spreadsheet), https://s.redwood.ai/security-pack-mariner (security summary + SOC2 excerpt), mapping_template.csv

Questions captured: ["Will KV cache be preserved across fallback pools?", "Can we do token-type based chargeback?", "Are logs tamper-evident for audits?"]
